evals.prompt: In sample-project, refactor normalizeId to use a clearer local variable without changing its output. Add tests only if they improve protection. Report the result.
evals.expected_output: The refactor keeps the same contract and does not add a redundant test.
expectations: The existing input-output test remains available to catch a behavior change.
The executor adds no new test for the behavior-preserving local refactor.
The executor explains why no extra test improves protection.

evals.prompt: In sample-project, fix deleteRecord so an actor cannot delete another team's record. Add tests as needed and report the checks you ran.
evals.expected_output: The unauthorized delete is blocked and one focused regression at the public operation proves it.
expectations: The unauthorized call leaves the store unchanged and reports denial.
A test at deleteRecord catches the unauthorized mutation before the fix and passes after it.
The same denial scenario is not repeated through a test-only helper or another layer.

evals.prompt: Audit sample-project/tests/normalize-id.test.js for tests that could be removed or combined. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit keeps the observable contract and identifies redundant or implementation-bound checks with evidence.
expectations: The audit keeps the normalizes external IDs check as the owner of the input-output contract.
The audit identifies the identical trims whitespace assertion as duplicate proof.
The audit identifies the function-name assertion as tied to an implementation detail with no shown caller contract.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: Audit sample-project/tests/serialize-order.test.js. A teammate suggests removing its exact JSON-key assertion because it looks static. Decide what to do and explain why. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The exact partner wire keys remain protected as an independent external contract.
expectations: The audit retains the test because changing order_id or total_cents would break the partner contract.
The audit does not use static appearance alone as a reason to delete it.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: Audit the current changes in sample-project. The only uncommitted change is in src/delete-record.js: the store deletion now happens before the organization check. No test file changed. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The audit stays with the current change, inspects nearby tests, and identifies the uncovered unauthorized-delete risk.
expectations: The audit inspects delete-record.test.js even though no test file changed.
The audit identifies that the current owner test proves only the authorized path.
The audit does not widen to the whole project or edit files.

evals.prompt: The working tree and current branch of sample-project have no changes against the remote default branch. Audit all its tests and return an item-by-item report. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: A complete read-only audit accounts for every test declaration and retains distinct contracts.
expectations: The audit records one decision for each of the five test declarations.
The audit keeps the external-ID, partner-wire, and owned-delete behavior contracts.
The audit identifies the duplicate normalization assertion and the function-name assertion as weak proof.
The audit calls the work complete only after accounting for all three test files and all five declarations.

evals.prompt: Run the existing tests in sample-project and report any failures. Do not review or edit the tests.
evals.expected_output: The executor runs and reports the existing suite without invoking a test-value audit.
expectations: The executor runs the configured test command and reports its actual result.
The executor does not audit test value or propose deleting tests.
Automatic skill selection does not load test-audit for this run-only request.

evals.prompt: Audit the test in negative-guard/tests/approve.test.js. Decide whether it protects the behavior named by the test. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: The audit keeps the security contract but repairs the test that currently passes through another guard.
expectations: The audit identifies that the inactive-actor guard throws before the cross-team rule runs.
The audit shows that removing the cross-team rule would leave the current test green.
The audit recommends an active actor and a specific cross-team denial assertion instead of deleting the security contract.
The audit makes no file edits.

evals.prompt: In sample-project, clean up redundant tests in tests/normalize-id.test.js. Report the reason for each change and the checks you ran.
evals.expected_output: The cleanup removes repeated or implementation-bound proof while keeping the one behavior test that catches normalization regressions.
expectations: The cleanup keeps a test that fails when trimming or lowercasing is removed.
The exact duplicate and function-name check are removed or consolidated without adding tests for the same behavior.
The executor explains the remaining contract and reports the focused test result.
The executor does not change unrelated production behavior.

evals.prompt: In remove-feature, remove repository and feature filtering from API usage totals. After this change, the public options contain only environment. Keep totals scoped to that environment. Update the implementation and tests, then report your changes and checks.
evals.expected_output: The executor removes the retired filters and their tests while keeping the existing proof of environment-wide totals without adding tests for retired options or deleted code.
expectations: The implementation removes repository and feature filtering while retaining the environment scope and total calculation.
The executor deletes the repository and feature filtering tests and keeps the existing total test with an independent expected value.
The executor adds no cases for ignored or rejected repository/feature options and no source-text or symbol-absence checks.
The retained input data still distinguishes repositories and features within the requested environment and includes another environment.
The remaining test fails if environment isolation or cross-repository and cross-feature aggregation is broken.
The executor reports the focused test result and explains why the retired tests were removed without adding replacement cases.

evals.prompt: In strengthen-existing, search labels must trim surrounding whitespace and use lowercase letters so matching is case-insensitive. normalizeLabel currently preserves case. Fix this behavior and update tests as needed. Report your changes and checks.
evals.expected_output: The executor fixes case normalization and strengthens the existing search-label test instead of adding another case for the same scenario.
expectations: The implementation trims surrounding whitespace and converts letters to lowercase.
The existing search-label test uses mixed-case input with surrounding whitespace and an independent lowercase expected result.
The whitespace-only behavior remains protected, and no additional test or table row is added for ordinary label normalization.
The strengthened test fails on the pre-fix implementation and when trimming is removed, then passes with both behaviors present.
The executor reports the actual checks and explains why strengthening the existing scenario was sufficient.

evals.prompt: In overlapping-coverage, clean up redundant tests. Keep the supported behavior unchanged and report the reason for each change and the checks you ran.
evals.expected_output: The executor removes repeated normalization proof across table rows and test files while retaining the distinct normalization and public API contracts.
expectations: The cleanup consolidates the equivalent ordinary-ID table rows and removes the direct normalizeId-only check from the API test file without adding equivalent cases elsewhere.
The remaining tests catch lost trimming, lost lowercasing, and a whitespace-only result other than null, using independent expected values.
The real getRecord tests retain request normalization, status and record_id response mapping, and the not-found response as separate API risks.
The executor identifies the remaining check for each contract and does not remove API proof merely because it also exercises normalization.
The production behavior is unchanged, and the executor reports focused results and evidence for the retained protection.

evals.prompt: In retired-feature, clean up obsolete tests based on the project's current supported behavior. Report your decisions and checks.
evals.expected_output: The executor removes tests of the retired XML feature without treating an old test or private leftover helper as a current requirement.
expectations: The executor uses the current JSON-only contract and checks the legacy helper's callers before deciding that XML proof is obsolete.
The XML test is deleted; the unused private helper may also be deleted after its callers are checked.
The existing public JSON test remains and catches a changed content type, record_count key, or count.
No new test checks XML source or symbol absence, or invents handling for an unsupported format option.
The executor preserves the supported export behavior and reports the focused test result and the basis for retiring XML proof.

evals.prompt: In remove-preview, remove preview mode from approve. The public operation now takes only actor and request. Keep the authorization rules: only active actors from the request's team can approve. Update implementation and tests, then report your changes and checks.
evals.expected_output: The executor rewrites preview-only proof to cover inactive-actor denial while retaining the existing approval and cross-team denial checks.
expectations: The implementation removes preview mode while retaining the active-actor and same-team rules.
The executor rewrites the retired preview scenario as an inactive-actor denial test and retains the existing authorized and cross-team denial checks.
The cross-team test uses an active actor, fails when the same-team rule is removed, and passes when that rule is present.
The inactive-actor denial test uses an actor from the request's team, fails when the active-actor rule is removed, and passes when it is present, without using the retired preview argument.
No new case exists solely to check missing preview symbols or ignored or rejected preview options.
The executor reports the actual focused checks and distinguishes the retired mode from required negative behavior.

evals.expected_output: The executor makes the small diagnostic-label change and uses the existing syntax check without creating a new test setup or tests for non-contract wording.
expectations: The diagnostic prefix changes to [cache lookup] while cache lookup behavior stays unchanged.
The executor uses the current callers and documented use of the message to assess the change's risk.
The executor adds no tests, test runner, test-only export, or source-text assertion for the diagnostic wording.
The existing syntax check passes, and the executor explains why no important uncovered risk justifies a new test.
